patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.
patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Uncomplicated pregnancy leading up to a vaginal delivery. No significant past medical or surgical history.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. Lives with her partner.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Complains of minor difficulty in breathing but denies any urinary pain, headache, vomiting, or diarrhea.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and manage a patient presenting with postpartum fever and abdominal tenderness.

turns.content: Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—first, when was your delivery (how many days ago), and do you have a measured fever (highest temperature)? Patient: Doctor: Any uterine/abdominal tenderness plus foul-smelling lochia or heavy bleeding, and did you have C-section or other risk factors (prolonged labor/ruptured membranes)?

Patient: I delivered about 3 days ago, and my temperature has been around 38.5°C. I’ve had significant uterine tenderness, and I did have a prolonged labor. My urination has felt more frequent as well.

Doctor: Thanks—do you have **foul-smelling lochia or heavy postpartum bleeding**, and have you felt **shaking chills** or had **any wound redness/pus** from an incision (if C-section) or perineal area? Doctor: Also, do you have **lower abdominal pain vs. costovertebral/flank pain**, and are you having **burning with urination** suggesting a UTI?

I haven’t noticed foul-smelling lochia, but my bleeding has felt heavier than expected at times, and I’ve had chills. My lower abdominal pain is more of a deep uterine tenderness, and I don’t have burning when I urinate. I haven’t had any wound redness or pus since delivery.

Doctor: Given postpartum day 3 with 38.5°C fever, uterine (deep) tenderness, and chills without urinary burning or incision infection, I’m concerned for **postpartum endometritis**—can you confirm whether your lochia is foul-smelling (even intermittently) and whether you have had nausea or uterine subinvolution? Doctor: REQUEST TEST: CBC, Urinalysis, and Blood cultures (before antibiotics). Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Pelvic exam/ultrasound for retained products if bleeding remains heavy.

RESULTS: Temperature 102°F (38.9°C); BP 118/78 mmHg; Heart rate 111/min; Respiratory rate 17/min; O2 saturation 98% on room air. CBC: WBC pending, Hemoglobin pending, Platelets pending. Urinalysis: appearance/WBC/RBC/nitrites/leukocyte esterase pending. Abdominal exam: non-distended abdomen, decreased bowel sounds, tympanic percussion throughout, tender uterus. Pulmonary exam: minor bibasilar crackles, no respiratory distress signs. Blood cultures: pending.

Doctor: With postpartum day 3 fever to 38.9°C plus uterine tenderness and chills, and no clear urinary burning or incision infection, this is most consistent with **postpartum endometritis**; I want you to do a pelvic assessment to check uterine subinvolution and lochia character while we’re ruling out retained products—will you allow a pelvic exam and uterine palpation now? Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Pelvic exam (lochia odor, uterine subinvolution, cervical motion tenderness) + Transvaginal pelvic ultrasound for retained products; once CBC/UA come back, we’ll start broad-spectrum antibiotics promptly.

RESULTS: Temperature 102°F (38.9°C); BP 118/78 mmHg; Heart rate 111/min; Respiratory rate 17/min; Oxygen saturation 98% on room air. CBC: WBC pending, Hemoglobin pending, Platelets pending. Urinalysis: appearance/WBC/RBC/nitrites/leukocyte esterase pending. Abdominal exam: non-distended abdomen; decreased bowel sounds; tympanic percussion throughout; tender uterus. Pulmonary exam: minor bibasilar crackles, no signs of respiratory distress. Blood cultures: pending.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—before we start treatment, do you have **foul-smelling lochia** right now or at any point since delivery, and are you having **uterine/fundal tenderness that worsens with movement**? Also, is there any **history of prolonged rupture of membranes** or **chorioamnionitis** during labor. Doctor: While we confirm retained products, I’m ordering **REQUEST TEST: Broad-spectrum postpartum endometritis antibiotic timing confirmation + start empiric therapy after cultures (e.g., clindamycin + gentamicin)** and I’ll proceed with a **pelvic exam** to check lochia odor, cervical motion tenderness, and uterine subinvolution. Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum endometritis (postpartum uterine infection)
